name: kitchen appliances · one day
what: One row is one appliance monitored for a day: power drawn every two minutes for 24 hours. One column is one two-minute reading, in clock order from midnight.
why: Overnight a washing machine, a dryer and a dishwasher all draw nothing, so they are indistinguishable. They separate during the day's usage peaks and merge again at night.

name: eye writing · vertical
what: One row is one trial: a person writing a Japanese katakana stroke with their eyes, recorded as the vertical position of the gaze at 1 kHz. One column is one millisecond of that movement.
why: Every stroke starts from the same fixation point. At the beginning the six strokes are physically identical and no clustering can separate them; they fan apart as the stroke is drawn. Concepts emerging, in the literal sense.
source: UCR/UEA time series classification archive (Fang & Shinozaki)

name: arcene · mass spectrometry
what: One row is one patient: mass-spectrometry intensities used to tell cancer from healthy tissue.
why: Columns are mass-charge positions, in no order that means anything: column 7 is not earlier than column 8. Walking them imposes an arrival order the data never had, which is why shuffling the columns changes nothing.
source: ASU feature selection repository / NIPS 2003 challenge
